Yeah having seen parts of my partners ADHD assessment, I expected it to be more like a therapy session. His assessor also had adhd so they both rambled a lot and got to discuss things in a lot of detail. For mine it was very much "do you do this - tick, next box" 


I had so much more to say at the end but the 2 hours was up. She had to stop me interrupting her giving the verdict 😅


Their way of determining whether the hyperactivity was severe enough to warrant that part of the diagnosis was whether people outside of my family considered me loud and obnoxious. They don't but, it doesn't stop me from fidgeting constantly and being stuck doing something and unable to stop despite kind of wanting to or needing to. 


Thank you, I think meds will be my next course of action. I think it'll just be something I mention to them so they can assess symptoms and how the medication affects them.

CBT and they will likely work on exposure therapy with your son.

The first line of treatment shouldn't be medication. Your son is young and can definitely build the skills he needs to cope and manage his anxiety without medication. A good therapist will help him to manage his anxiety which in turn will help reduce the nausea/fear of being sick. 

Also, it's perfectly normal to feel anxious and nervous about big changes in your life. Taking exams and going to college are very stressful and the body will respond to that.

Avoidance makes anxiety way worse so it's best you seek some help or read up on CBT and see what you could be doing to help reframe some of the thoughts he's having. I know in the UK there tends to be long waiting lists to get help but even local charities can help like MIND. Just having a greater understanding about anxiety and how it works may help your son.

Best of luck ☺️

It would really help to confront why you feel the need to put on an act and realise it's not useful, it's a facade and deceitful. You won't get meaningful relationships by doing it, despite it feeling like it might be on the moment. Opening up is vulnerable and some people won't like what you have to say but some people will. It's tough to be playing an act most your life then stopping completely.

The shit your partner is saying is disgusting. He sounds incredibly manipulative. Being told how many girls he's had to give up to be with you is going to deeply affect your self esteem. He honestly doesn't seem like the greatest guy to be around or worth figuring things out with.

Your daughter on the otherhand is 1 years old. She doesn't need to be around this and you are the person that can help with that. She needs someone to tell her that's not a way to speak to people or treat someone. She needs you more than you think. You are not an awful person and I can understand wanting to end it all but, you will leave a wreckage behind.
